sparql:
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX dtl: <http://www.DTL.org/schema/properties/>
PREFIX mo: <http://purl.org/ontology/mo/>
PREFIX foaf: <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/>
SELECT DISTINCT ?composer 
 WHERE {
 ?composer rdf:type mo:MusicArtist .
 ?composer foaf:name "%s" .
 ?tune rdf:type mo:MusicalWork .
 ?tune dtl:composed_by ?composer .
 }
gold_question: Is there more than one composer with this name in the graph?

model_output.nl_question: Which composer with the given name has composed at least one musical work?
model_output.confidence_rationale: No NL evidence aligns with the composition intent, so the question is generated from the SPARQL. The query clearly filters a music artist by the given name and requires that they have composed at least one musical work, then returns that composer.

sparql:
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX dtl: <http://www.DTL.org/schema/properties/>
PREFIX mo: <http://purl.org/ontology/mo/>
PREFIX foaf: <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/>
SELECT DISTINCT ?arranger 
 WHERE {
 ?arranger rdf:type mo:MusicArtist .
 ?arranger foaf:name "%s" .
 ?tune rdf:type mo:MusicalWork .
 ?tune dtl:arranged_by ?arranger .
 }
gold_question: Is there more than one arranger with this name in the graph?

review.note: This could be name disambiguation on the one hand - is there more than one arranger with this name in the dataset. Or, on the other hand, it could be a check whether there is an arranger with this name (this is what was generated), or whether this musician did any arrangements. The presence of 'distinct' suggests the former I would say.

model_output.nl_question: Which musician with the given name arranged at least one musical work?
model_output.confidence_rationale: No provided evidence aligns with arranging; the query clearly selects the musician resource with the given name who is linked as the arranger of a musical work. The question is directly derived from the SPARQL structure.

sparql:

PREFIX mo: <http://purl.org/ontology/mo/>
PREFIX foaf: <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/>
SELECT ?band 
 WHERE {
 ?band rdf:type mo:MusicGroup .
 ?band foaf:name "%s" .
 }
gold_question: Find the band by its name

model_output.nl_question: Which music group (band) has the given name?
model_output.confidence_rationale: There is no usable evidence matching this simple lookup, but the SPARQL clearly returns the music group whose foaf:name equals a provided string. The generated question directly reflects that intent.

sparql:
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX dc: <http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/>
PREFIX mo: <http://purl.org/ontology/mo/>
SELECT ?trackt ?signal
 WHERE {
 ?track rdf:type mo:Track .
 ?track dc:title ?trackt .
 ?track mo:track_number "%i" .
 ?medium mo:track ?track .
 ?medium dc:title ?mediumt .
 ?medium mo:record_number "%i" .
 ?release mo:record ?medium .
 ?release dc:title "%s" .
 ?signal mo:published_as ?track .
 }
gold_question: Given the album title, disk number and track number, find the track title and the associated signal

review.note: My main concern here is the album vs release difference - in NL we would talk about album title rather than release title; in the ontology, release was chosen rather than album to indicate the relation to time

model_output.nl_question: For the specified release title, record number, and track number, what is the track title and the corresponding audio signal published as that track?
model_output.confidence_rationale: The SPARQL clearly filters by a given release title, record number, and track number, and returns the track title along with the signal published as that track. No provided evidence directly matches this intent, so the question is generated from the query structure.

sparql:
PREFIX dtl: <http://www.DTL.org/schema/properties/>
PREFIX event: <http://purl.org/NET/c4dm/event.owl#>
PREFIX mo: <http://purl.org/ontology/mo/>
SELECT DISTINCT ?musician 
## WHERE {
## ?session mo:performer <%s> .
## ?session event:sub_event ?performance .
## ?performance mo:performer ?performer .
## ?performer dtl:musician ?musician .
## }
gold_question: Which musicians performed together with the given performer?

review.note: Missing context - the Jazz Ontology models all performances as part of a session, therefore this query is for all musicians who ever performed together with the given one

model_output.nl_question: Which musicians performed in the session featuring the given performer?
model_output.confidence_rationale: The SPARQL selects musicians from performances that are sub-events of a session where a given performer participated, which aligns with the idea of a band line-up. However, the evidence mentions a single performance rather than a session, and the WHERE block is commented, introducing some ambiguity.

retained_evidence_phrases.text: What is the band line-up for the given performance?

sparql:
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX dc: <http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/>
PREFIX dtl: <http://www.DTL.org/schema/properties/>
PREFIX event: <http://purl.org/NET/c4dm/event.owl#>
PREFIX mo: <http://purl.org/ontology/mo/>
PREFIX tl: <http://purl.org/NET/c4dm/timeline.owl#>
PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>
PREFIX foaf: <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/>
SELECT ?bandname ?performance_title ?startdate
?solostart ?solo_instrument_label ?soloist_name
WHERE {
?performance rdf:type mo:Performance .
?performance dc:title ?performance_title .
?session event:sub_event ?performance .
?session event:time ?date .
?date tl:at ?startdate .
?session mo:performer ?band .
?band foaf:name ?bandname .
?performance event:sub_event ?solo .
?solo event:time ?solotime .
?solotime tl:beginsAt ?solostart .
?solotime tl:endsAt ?soloend .
?solo dtl:solo_instrument ?solo_instrument .
?solo_instrument dtl:dtl_inst_label
?solo_instrument_label .
?solo dtl:solo_performer ?soloperformer .
?soloperformer dtl:musician ?soloist .
?soloist foaf:name ?soloist_name .
}
gold_question: List all solos with attributed solo performers, with the track title and date, solo timestamp and instrument

model_output.nl_question: Which performances have solos with attributed musicians, and for each solo what are its start time, instrument, and soloist, along with the performance title, band name, and date?
model_output.confidence_rationale: CQ7 directly matches the core intent of retrieving performances with solos that have attributed musicians, and CQ6 supports the inclusion of solo timestamps. The final question paraphrases these and incorporates additional fields (performance title, band name, date) that are clearly selected in the SPARQL.

retained_evidence_phrases.text: Find all performances which have solos with attributed musicians
Find all solos and their timestamps in a performance

gold_question: List all places in the graph with their coordinates

review.note: The generated phrase is factually accurate but highly improbable in NL.

model_output.nl_question: Which places have geocoordinates (latitude and longitude) and labels?
model_output.confidence_rationale: The SPARQL selects all mtp:Location resources that have a label and both latitude and longitude. The only aligned evidence is a query comment indicating the scope is places; the detailed constraints (coordinates) come directly from the SPARQL.

sparql:
PREFIX mtp: <http://w3id.org/polifonia/ontology/meetups-ontology#>
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>

SELECT DISTINCT ?subjectID ?subjectLabel
WHERE {
 ?meetupID mtp:hasSubject ?subjectID .
 ?subjectID rdfs:label ?subjectLabel
}
LIMIT 10
gold_question: Give me ten examples of subjects from the graph?

model_output.nl_question: What are the names of up to 10 subjects associated with meetups?
model_output.confidence_rationale: The question is derived directly from the SPARQL, which selects distinct meetup subjects and their labels with a limit of 10. No usable natural-language evidence aligns with this specific intent, so confidence is moderated.

gold_question: List all organs in the graph

model_output.nl_question: What are the names of all organs?
model_output.confidence_rationale: No provided evidence matches the query’s intent. The SPARQL clearly selects all entities of type organ:Organ and their rdfs:label, so the generated question reflects listing all organs by name.

gold_question: List the descriptions of the specified organs

model_output.nl_question: What are the names of the specified organs?
model_output.confidence_rationale: No provided evidence matches this query’s intent. The SPARQL clearly retrieves rdfs:label values for three specified organ entities, so the question is generated directly from the query semantics.

gold_question: Which of the listed organs have an external website?

model_output.nl_question: What are the descriptions for the given organs?
model_output.confidence_rationale: The SPARQL clearly retrieves values of core:description for a specified set of organ entities. No provided evidence directly addresses descriptions or external links for organs, so the question is generated from the query structure.
